hero.role: PIBIC/CNPq Undergraduate Researcher · Empirical Software Engineering
hero.statement: I study how empirical and qualitative methods produce grounded knowledge about software engineering. My work combines interview-based inquiry, literature synthesis, and automated research software.

approach.title: Research orientation
approach.lead: Understanding how methodological choices shape what we observe, interpret, and claim about software engineering phenomena.

items.title: Qualitative and empirical methodology
items.text: My primary focus lies in research methods, especially qualitative inquiry, Reflexive Thematic Analysis, and the epistemological commitments behind empirical evidence. I am interested in how structured analytical procedures uncover patterns and mechanisms across real contexts.

items.title: Evidence synthesis and Open Science
items.text: Conducting Multivocal Literature Reviews that combine academic and grey literature under auditable protocols. I organize traceable datasets and open codebooks so analytical decisions remain inspectable.

items.title: Open interdisciplinary agenda
items.text: Recent studies examined tech recruitment as an initial empirical domain rather than a fixed thematic boundary. My agenda remains open to sociotechnical questions across developer practices, AI consequences, computing education, health systems, and open source communities.

publications.title: Publications and manuscripts
publications.lead: Peer-reviewed publications, manuscripts under revision, and ongoing secondary studies.

chase2026.venue: Proceedings of the 19th International Conference on Cooperative and Human Aspects of Software Engineering (CHASE 2026), co-located with ICSE 2026.
chase2026.abstract: Qualitative interview study with 22 early-career software engineers examining over 470 online hiring experiences through Applicant Attribution-Reaction Theory (AART), synthesizing 22 constructive patterns for human-centered recruitment practices.

emse2026.venue: Under second-round review at Empirical Software Engineering (EMSE-D-25-00839R1).
emse2026.abstract: Qualitative investigation of negative online hiring experiences reported by 22 early-career Brazilian software engineers, identifying 25 anti-patterns across 10 analytical themes through Reflexive Thematic Analysis and AART, accompanied by an open codebook and interactive web panel.

mlr2026.title: Multivocal Literature Review on Recruitment and Selection in Software Engineering
mlr2026.venue: Ongoing secondary study combining academic and grey literature.
mlr2026.abstract: Multi-source evidence synthesis mapping empirical and practitioner literature on software engineering recruitment and selection, currently undergoing screening verification and protocol auditing.

software.title: Research software
software.lead: Open research infrastructure and automated data pipelines built for reproducibility and community access.

datawashes.subtitle: GESID / Open API, automated pipeline, and dashboard
datawashes.lede: Public open-source API and web dashboard maintained by GESID for programmatic access to proceedings from the Workshop on Social, Human, and Economic Aspects of Software (WASHES). Its monthly pipeline scrapes SOL SBC records, classifies abstracts, updates citation counts, and deploys automatically.
datawashes.attribution: Institutional ownership belongs to GESID. Platform outputs are collaborative.
datawashes.role_text: Built Flask API routes and pytest unit tests during the UFCA extension project. Returned voluntarily one year later to refactor the frontend and optimize the dashboard using the official WASHES color palette, adapt CitationMiner to Python, and automate both monthly data updates and deployment to eliminate manual maintenance.
